newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - MoneyGram makes solid debut.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - MoneyGram makes solid debut.

text.p: MoneyGram Payment Systems Inc shares rose about 11 percent on their first day of trading on Wednesday.
Shares were up 1-3/8 to 13-3/8 on a volume of 3.4 million shares traded by the early afternoon. The issue was one of the most active on the big board.
"It's a nice pop in view of a collapsing market," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket. "It was priced to sell, and that's what its doing."
Last month, the price range on the 14.46 million share IPO was lowered to $10 to $12 per share from $15 to $17 per share. The issue was priced late on Tuesday at $12 a share.
The company, a non-bank provider of consumer money wire transfer services, is being divested from First Data Corp.
Morgan Stanley was lead underwriter on the deal.
Shares of Vivid Technologies Inc were flat at their IPO price of $12, after reaching a high earlier in the day of 12-1/2.
The estimated range on the two million share issue was $12 to $14 a share. The lead underwriter was Lehman Brothers.
Vivid makes automated inspection systems which detect plastic and other explosives in airline baggage.
SkyMall Inc also made its debut on Wednesday, with shares climbing 3/4 to 8-3/4. The two million share IPO was priced at $8 a share in a deal led by Josephthal Lyon & Ross.
The in-flight catalog company sells merchandise provided by participating merchants to airline passengers.

Highway Holdings Ltd units slipped 3/8 from their IPO price of $5.50 a unit to 5-1/8. The issue was to debut yesterday but was delayed because of a "document holdup", according to underwriter H.J. Meyers & Co.
Each of the 1.05 million units consists of one share and one warrant. The company makes a variety of metal parts and components.
